subject: psychology
title: Attachment Theory: Exam-Style Stretch
welcome_lead: Separate deprivation from privation and evaluate Bowlby.
meta_desc: GCSE Psychology exam stretch on attachment: Romanian orphans, privation and evaluation of Bowlby.
final_note: You can argue both sides of Bowlby's claims with evidence.

concepts.def: Losing an attachment that did form.

walkthroughs.body_html: Deprivation = losing an attachment that already formed (e.g. hospital stay). Privation = no attachment ever formed (e.g. early institutional care). Rutter argued Bowlby's 44 Thieves better fits privation than deprivation.

Rutter followed children adopted from Romanian orphanages. Those adopted before 6 months caught up well; those adopted after 2 years showed lasting attachment problems (e.g. disinhibited attachment). Recovery is possible but limited.

Strengths: huge impact on hospital and adoption practice; supported by Ainsworth's work. Weaknesses: ignores the role of fathers; monotropy may be overstated; 44 Thieves was retrospective and confounded privation with deprivation.
